plain_twins.meandiff_k1: switch on when mean(full-throttle overestimate) minus mean(rest) > 0.10; the ramp at that difference, k = 1; a program of its own
plain_twins.meandiff_limit: the same switch turning on the hand-set range limit; switched off it is the no-caution actor; a hinge program of its own when on

arms.programs: step 2's own programs for BCA's switched ramp and the plumbing check; a refused arm's place keeps a height-0 copy, never saved or scored

choices.choice: C2's margins, statistic, alpha, seeds-ahead rule, multiplicity and noise floor

claims.C1: step 2's three go marks in the main setting (version 8's claim 4), unchanged: net lead at least 10, keeps at most 3 lost, even pull beaten by at least 15
claims.C2: BCA's switched ramp beats each plain twin (split-conformal switch, mean-difference switch with the ramp, mean-difference switch with the hand-set range limit), paired by seed on the net across worlds

compute.memory_rule: version 7's, unchanged: a phase starts only if the reserved peaks of the running phases plus its own are at most WSL's MemTotal minus 8 GiB, and MemAvailable is at least its own reservation plus 8 GiB; an unmeasured phase kind reserves 7 GiB; a measured kind 1.25 x its measured peak; policy phases max(7 GiB, 2 x measured peak)
compute.source: version 8's ledger, main setting, seeds 11 and 14: 1.51-1.54 CPU-hours per seed

departures: BCA's groups are pooled from every held-out recorded row outside the ball (version 8: survivors and the calibration bank only)
a refusal fails only the arms that need BCA (version 8: the whole actor phase of the seed stopped)
the plain twins are trained arms; C2 is new
the near-80 band, the random-rows control, version 6's band, the readouts and version 8's exploratory stop rules are removed
the data record's run sizes are read back under the key run_sizes (the cause of version 8's amendment 1)
host: TD3+BC, actor only (step 2's protocol): alpha 5.0, 20,000 actor steps in chunks of 4,000, 100,000 critic updates

kill_rules.budget: a stage past twice its forecast, or the run past the cap, pauses until budget-continue is typed
kill_rules.no_training: the frozen code's no-training checks on seeds 0-4 (commands only) must all pass, or the design is redrafted
kill_rules.phase_stop: a stopped phase is not rerun; every mark that needs it fails
kill_rules.reproduction: the plumbing's reproduction on seed 0 must hold, or no result stands

label: Version 9, near-80 deciding test: the main setting on fresh seeds, BCA's two groups pooled from every held-out recorded row outside the ball
measures: points per arm, world, seed and situation; the net across worlds (strong current); held-to-70%, capped-at-80% points and the share of steps past 80% (reported)
no_training_facts_seeds_0_4: computed by freeze.py with the frozen code (code/facts_v9.py, commands only) and pinned in prereg.json

outcome_free_count.check: the switch phase must find exactly the counted sizes
outcome_free_count.rule: the pooled full-throttle and rest groups counted per seed-world from commands alone in the data phase, before any training, beside BCA's certifiable bar of 36 rows; reported, never a stop

pooled_groups.every_switch_arm: reads the same two groups, scored once by the switch phase
pooled_groups.full_throttle: the survivors (kept training rows past t_lo) plus the held-out rows past t_lo
pooled_groups.heldout: every row of the calibration split and the evaluation split whose command lies outside the ball (the bank is part of the calibration split)
pooled_groups.rest: the held-out rows at or below t_lo
pooled_groups.scored_tests: no scored number reads these rows: every score is a rollout from the four fixed test start sets
unchanged: BCA's certificate (alpha 0.1, credibility 0.95, 1,000 draws, q05 above 0.10)

question: In the main test's setting, on seeds nobody has seen, with BCA's two groups built from every held-out recorded row outside the ball, does BCA's switched ramp still meet step 2's three marks (C1), and does it beat the plain rules that read the same groups (C2)?

refusal_rule.obca_forced: takes the stalling world's height in both worlds, so a stalling-world refusal fails it in both
refusal_rule.rule: when BCA refuses in a seed-world (switch on, height not finite), obca_k1, obca_k2, obca_forced and the matched rivals (standin, even_pull, push_less, random_1, random_2) fail that seed; every other arm trains and is scored; no whole seed is stopped for a refusal

request: build now we need to keep pushing for good results. ASAP (20 October 2026, after version 8's claim 4 failed)

seeds.failed_seed: a seed whose data or a needed phase failed, or where BCA refused, fails every mark that needs it; never replaced

settings.main: the main test's removal of the densest 15% of recorded commands (the ball) from training and from BCA's calibration bank; no other removal
